elements.text: The Analogy: Global Mail vs. Office Intercom
Imagine a massive corporate building. Every desk has an internal extension number (Private IP), but the building itself has only one official street address (Public IP).

segments.speech: To understand why we need both public and private IP addresses, let's use an everyday analogy. Imagine a massive corporate building. Inside the building, everyone uses internal extension numbers to talk to each other—those are like Private IP addresses. But when the company sends a letter to someone outside, it must use the building's single official street address—that's a Public IP address. Does that make sense so far?

elements.text: What is a Private IP Address?
Private IPs are used inside a local network. They are not routable on the public internet.
Many homes and offices reuse the exact same private IP addresses safely!

segments.speech: Let's look more closely at private IP addresses. These are numbers assigned to devices inside your home or office network, like 192.168.1.5. Does that make sense so far, Roosevelt?
